methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort of only 66 patients with 15 cancer-specific deaths, with no reported power calculation or validation cohort. Dichotomization cutoffs for CD4+, CD8+, CD68+, and TICD were derived by ROC on the same outcome used for survival analysis, which inflates associations and biases Kaplan-Meier/Cox results; no correction (splitting, bootstrap, cross-validation) is described. The multivariate Cox model yielded extreme and unstable estimates (HR 30.8, 95% CI 6.39-148 for TICD; HR 12.7, 95% CI 3.01-53.5 for lymphatic invasion), reflecting over-fitting given the events-per-variable ratio; the authors themselves flag model stability concerns. Hotspot fields were manually selected and no blinded scoring, inter-observer agreement, multiplicity correction (four markers x two regions), or sensitivity analyses are reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is an individual retrospective cohort of consecutive Stage II-III OCRC patients at one center with cancer-specific survival as endpoint, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b (bordering on 4 given small N and retrospective single-center design). The clinical question - risk-stratifying an underserved OCRC subset - is meaningful, and the invasive-front immune contexture is a patient-relevant correlate of CSS. However, the findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing: cutoffs are data-derived and unvalidated, there is no comparison with Immunoscore or standard prognostic tools, and no clinical decision pathway is operationalized. The SEMS-vs-TDT immune-density signal is intriguing but is appropriately flagged by the authors as requiring prospective, ideally randomized validation.

reporting_quality.justification: As a tumor-biomarker prognostic study, REMARK is the most applicable checklist (STROBE also partially relevant). The manuscript provides a clear patient flow diagram with inclusion/exclusion counts, specifies staining antibodies and conditions (Table S1), defines endpoints, and describes analysis software, but it omits several REMARK items: no protocol registration or pre-specified cutoffs, no description of blinded assessment, no handling of missing data, no reporting on inter-observer or technical replicates for hotspot selection, and no explicit variable-selection rationale for the Cox model. No data-availability or code-availability statement is present in the blinded text, and no repository or script is referenced; raw per-case immune-cell densities are not provided.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily population-focused: multiplex-IF characterization of CD4+/CD8+/CD68+ cells specifically in obstructive CRC, a subset less studied than conventional CRC. Prognostic value of TILs and TAMs at the invasive front is well established in CRC (Immunoscore - Pages et al. 2018; Wankhede 2025; multiple TAM meta-analyses), so the mechanistic and empirical findings are confirmatory rather than conceptually new. The SEMS-vs-TDT immune-density comparison and the observation of exaggerated center-to-invasive-front gradients in OCRC are the most original contributions, but both are preliminary. Overall this is a meaningful but incremental extension of the Immunoscore paradigm into an understudied OCRC niche.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized, with an informative abstract that is quantitatively grounded (specific HR, cell densities, and p-values). The Introduction sets up the OCRC-specific knowledge gap, Methods describe the multiplex IF workflow in reproducible detail, Results follow the logical arc of spatial distribution to prognosis to clinicopathological correlation to device comparison, and Discussion appropriately situates findings against the Immunoscore literature and acknowledges key limitations. Figure captions are self-contained and numerically aligned with text. Minor issues: some long sentences in the Discussion, and the Statistical Analysis section is placed after Conclusions rather than within Methods.

key_strengths: Addresses a genuine clinical gap by profiling the immune microenvironment of obstructive CRC, an understudied oncologic-emergency subset
Well-executed multiplex immunofluorescence workflow with clear marker panel (CD4/CD8/CD68/CK/aSMA/DAPI) and tissue-segmentation pipeline
Clear reporting of patient flow, cohort definition, and center-versus-invasive-front comparison with concrete cell-density values
Novel exploratory observation that SEMS versus TDT decompression correlates with invasive-front TIL density, generating a testable hypothesis
key_concerns: ROC-derived cutoffs on the same outcome used for Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses create optimistic bias; no validation cohort or bootstrap/cross-validation is used
Severely underpowered multivariate Cox model (15 events, multiple covariates) yielding implausibly wide and unstable estimates (TICD HR 30.8, 95% CI 6.39-148)
Single-center retrospective design with N=66 and no reported power calculation, blinded scoring, inter-observer agreement, or multiplicity correction across markers and regions
REMARK adherence partial: no protocol pre-registration, no pre-specified cutoffs, no missing-data handling, no model-building rationale
No data- or code-availability statement; per-case density values and analysis scripts are not shared
Novelty is primarily populational (OCRC niche) rather than mechanistic or methodologic; findings largely confirm the established Immunoscore paradigm
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is a competent but methodologically fragile single-center retrospective biomarker analysis whose central effect estimates are inflated by data-derived cutoffs and overfitting; the content is appropriate for a tier-4 specialist/regional oncology journal with minor revisions, and would need expanded validation before tier-3 consideration.
